gap: No result ChatGPT got says the vívoactive 6 detects golf shots from the wrist sensors alone (it works best on the leading wrist, it does not detect putts, and it pairs with Approach CT10 club sensors). Together with its wrist heart-rate sensor, that is why it works as both a golf watch and a fitness tracker under $300, while the $299.99 Approach S44 has no heart-rate sensor.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited: Garmin's S44/S50 press release, Garmin's Which Watch golf comparison, the vívoactive 5 manual's Golf Menu and Playing Golf pages, the vívoactive 5 launch release, and our current page. Those cited pages already say the S44 has no wrist heart rate and the S50 adds it, and the vívoactive 5 Playing Golf page already says you need the Garmin Golf phone app before your first round. The vívoactive 6 Golf Menu page came up in ChatGPT's results but wasn't cited, and it only lists menu items. None of the pages state the vívoactive 6's automatic shot-detection limits (leading wrist, no putts) or its CT10 club-sensor support, and our page doesn't mention the vívoactive at all. Garmin's comparison page doesn't load its rows without JavaScript, so I couldn't read it directly. I'm relying on how ChatGPT used it.
decides: This supports the vívoactive line as the Garmin pick for 50/50 golf and fitness. The cheaper Garmin golf-first watches (S12, S44) can't track fitness because they have no optical heart-rate sensor. The first Approach with one is the S50 at $399.99 suggested retail, which is over budget. Meanwhile the vívoactive 6 has the golf features a golf-first buyer would miss: hazards on par 4s and 5s, layups, PinPointer, automatic shot detection and CT10 club tracking. Our rebuilt page should add a vívoactive row. For left-handers or people who wear a watch on their trailing wrist, it should say that automatic shot detection is designed around the leading wrist.
